1: Daily Study Bible · The Elect Lady · vv.1–3

Barclay says the writer is one of the last direct links with Jesus, that the elect lady is most likely a church, and that love and truth are joined in the opening verses; he notes that the greeting is a statement, not a wish, because John is sure of God’s gifts.

Says the elder has been understood from the earliest times to be the apostle John, that the lady may be a woman or a church, and that what binds Christians together is a common truth that abides in us and will be with us forever.
To the elect lady and her children

Some think that this and the following epistle are not of John the apostle, but of a certain presbyter John, whose tomb is shown to this day in Ephesus. Papias, too, the hearer of the apostles, and bishop in Hierapolis, often mentions him in his works. But now the general consensus of the Church holds that John the apostle also wrote these epistles, because they truly show much similarity in words and faith with his first epistle, and with similar zeal detest heretics.

Says John gives a slightly expanded form of the usual greeting, grace, mercy and peace, and that these are given in truth and love and cannot be had apart from them.

Since the heretics of that time, namely Marcian and Cerinthus, denied that our Lord Jesus Christ was truly the Son of God and attributed his beginning to human birth, John rightly recalls him as the Son of God the Father to refute these blasphemers.
4: Daily Study Bible · Trouble and Cure · vv.4–6

Barclay says some of the church were walking in the truth and some were not, and that John’s one cure for division is love, since only love can heal broken relationships and the proof of love for God is love for the brothers.
“I was very glad.” For certainly, the greatest cause of joy is to find someone who walks without offense in the straight path of faith in Christ according to His command.
5: Desiring God · Sermon · whole letter, centred on vv.5–7
Life Together at the End of the Age
Says John pleads rather than commands because a commandment the readers already knew still needed repeating, and that our love for one another is the measure of our Christian life.
The commandment to love one another

By this word, he reproaches the heretics, who were attempting to introduce new doctrines, leaving behind what they had heard from the apostles, and thereby disrupting the bonds of brotherly charity. Therefore, he says that he is by no means writing a new commandment but merely urging that the old faith and unblemished charity remain in all things.

Daily Study Bible · The Threatening Peril · vv.7–9

Barclay says the deceivers denied the reality of the incarnation, notes the shift in the Greek from past to present tense in the coming of Jesus, and reads going too far as the false teachers’ claim to be progressives, insisting that Jesus Christ must be the touchstone of all thinking.
Says the deceivers held that Jesus, being God, had only an apparent connection with the material world, and that John insists we confess Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh.
Many deceivers have gone out into the world
Therefore, I believe the beloved disciple used the word “to come,” not “to have come,” so that he might comprehend those denying both of the Lord's coming in the flesh.
8: “Truth: The Boundary of Love and the Test of Loyalty”
Says it is not enough to start out right, since we must finish in faith to receive a full reward.
Look to yourselves, that we do not lose those things we worked for

Therefore, John instructed them to beware of these: and he adds the reason: “Lest by adhering to them, you lose what you have previously worked for, but receive your full reward without any weakness.”
9: Daily Study Bible · The Threatening Peril · vv.7–9

Barclay says the deceivers denied the reality of the incarnation, notes the shift in the Greek from past to present tense in the coming of Jesus, and reads going too far as the false teachers’ claim to be progressives, insisting that Jesus Christ must be the touchstone of all thinking.
Says transgresses means going beyond a boundary, and that no one goes beyond the teaching of who Jesus is and what he has done, since to reject the true Jesus is to reject the Father and the Son.
Whoever transgresses and does not abide in the doctrine of Christ

He says that whoever does not remain in the teaching of Christ does not have God, but whoever remains in his teaching has both the Son and the Father, to show that the Father and the Son are one true God, and to convict those of falsehood who assert that the Son is either not God, or is posterior or inferior to the Father.
10: Daily Study Bible · No Compromise · vv.10–13

Barclay says refusing hospitality and even a greeting was the surest way to stop the false teachers, calls it an emergency rule, and holds that the church must still find a way to live with those who differ without breaking charity or being disloyal to the truth; he adds that the Greek for face to face is mouth to mouth.

Such caution did the apostles and their disciples use in religion at that time, that they would not permit even a word’s communion with any of those who had deviated from the truth; as Paul also says: A man that is heretical, after a first and second admonition, avoid, knowing that such a one is perverted and sins, being self-condemned (Tit. III).

Instructions for dealing with the false teachers

If anyone, he says, comes to you without this confession, not only will he not receive protection from you, but he will also not receive the prayer for salvation from you, rightly and cautiously saying this, as if this prayer for salvation is owed only to those who agree with us in morals and faith.
12: Says we can sympathize with John’s preference for speaking face to face rather than writing, though we are thankful for the letter.
The reason for the briefness of the letter, both in this and in the following one, is that John hoped to come to them and to add in person and by his presence what was lacking.

Barclay says refusing hospitality and even a greeting was the surest way to stop the false teachers, calls it an emergency rule, and holds that the church must still find a way to live with those who differ without breaking charity or being disloyal to the truth; he adds that the Greek for face to face is mouth to mouth.
Says the sister is most likely another church, and that the greeting is a reminder that true followers of Jesus are more than our own group and that defending the truth must not make us unloving.
The children of your elect sister

Just as he prohibits us to greet the adversaries of the truth, so, conversely, he greets the elect on behalf of the elect, so that the faithless may be detested by all the good, possibly to correct them in this way, and that the peace and love among the faithful may always increase.
